svg.text: The deploy control plane, end to end
Nine modules, what each one owns, and the specific December 2025 bug each one exists to prevent
our code
AWS managed
trade-off
what broke
verified
config.py — DeployConfig
The single source of truth
One frozen dataclass. Every name, size, port and model id.
Immutable: two callers cannot disagree about a name.
Validates the Fargate cpu/memory pair up front, because the API
error names neither the bad value nor the valid ones.
Holds NO account id. Never committed.
Dec 2025 had two YAMLs that disagreed: one made
finsights-cluster, the other deployed to finsights-cluster-new.
Teardown deleted the wrong one.
aws_session.py — AwsSession
Lazily built, shared everywhere
One boto3 Session; cached clients; identity on demand.
self._clients[service] = session.client(...)
account_id comes from STS at run time, so every ARN is built
for whoever is running the command.
Two credential worlds must both work: a laptop profile, and CI
env vars where no profile exists at all.
Naming a profile unconditionally breaks CI: boto3 raises
ProfileNotFound before it ever reads the environment.
policies.py — IamPolicies
Least privilege, written as data
Two documents: who may assume, and what they may do.
5 statements. No wildcard action. No Delete, anywhere.
A us.* model id is an inference profile, not a model. It needs
the profile ARN AND the foundation-model ARN in every region it
can route to.
Grant only us-east-1 and it works most of the time, then throws
AccessDenied when Bedrock routes elsewhere.
Region list read from GetInferenceProfile, not guessed.
provisioner.py — Provisioner
Converge, do not create
Six resources, created in dependency order, idempotently.
ECR x2, log group, 2 IAM roles, security group, cluster.
THE RULE: guard only what is not idempotent.
CreateRole -> guarded (EntityAlreadyExists)
AttachRolePolicy-> unconditional, every run
The old guard tested 1 thing but did 2. Role created, policy
attach failed -> every later run printed 'exists' and never
repaired it.
images.py — ImagePublisher
Subprocess as a typed method
Drives docker from Python: login, build, push.
docker build --platform linux/arm64 -f ... .
ECR password is a 12-hour token from the API, passed on stdin
so it never enters the process table.
ONE set of Dockerfiles, shared with local dev. Everything that
differs is injected, not built in.
If the image differed between local and cloud, the thing you
tested would not be the thing you deployed.
taskdef.py — TaskDefinitionBuilder
The correction to the fatal bug
Builds the RegisterTaskDefinition payload from code.
One task, two containers, one network namespace.
Health checks RESTATED here: Fargate ignores the image's
HEALTHCHECK entirely.
dependsOn HEALTHY reproduces compose's depends_on.
THIS is the file whose absence killed Dec 2025. The definition
lived only in a console, so the workflow could only
describe-then-patch. Account closed -> nothing could recreate it.
service.py — ServiceOperator
The lifecycle verbs
Register, create-or-update, scale, inspect, remove.
Polls for steady state instead of using the boto3 waiter, so
the REASON for a failure gets logged.
Reads the public IP from the task ENI on demand: with one task
and no load balancer, the IP genuinely changes.
Fargate bills per TASK, not per container. So a 2nd container is
~free and a 2nd task doubles the bill.
cli.py — DeploymentCli
Thin: it only wires and dispatches
preflight / up / status / smoke / logs / down / destroy
preflight INVOKES both Bedrock models rather than listing them;
a model can be listed and still not be usable.
down = desired count 0. No stopped-container charge exists on
Fargate, because there is no stopped container.
destroy removes even the images, for true zero.
All logic is runnable on a laptop. Every Dec 2025 bug would have
been visible if it had been.
VERIFIED, not asserted
Every claim above was observed
Query answered on ECS: $0.0140, 12,670 tokens, 9,631 ms.
Log said 'using IAM role' + 'S3_STREAMING mode'.
POST /query 200 OK from 127.0.0.1 — the wiring proof.
Polars object_store resolved the task role. This was the biggest
open risk: it does its own credential lookup, separate from
botocore.
destroy -> empty on all 6 checks -> up rebuilt to steady state.
That round trip is the real IaC test.
down reached desired=0 running=0. ECR left: 0.643 GB.
The one idea that ties all nine boxes together

Infrastructure that exists only in a cloud console is not infrastructure you own. Each module above turns a click into a value in a file, so the repository becomes the source of truth and AWS holds a copy
— rather than AWS holding the truth and the repository holding a patch script. The test of whether you got it right is not that deploy works; it is that destroy-then-deploy works.
FinSights on AWS ECS Fargate | verified 2026-07-31, account 908877262866 | source: ModelPipeline/deploy_aws/
